questions.q: In this lesson's worked data model, how is OpportunityLineItem related to Opportunity?
options: Master-Detail -- a line item cannot exist without its Opportunity, and deleting the Opportunity deletes its line items
Lookup -- a line item can exist with no Opportunity linked
Many-to-many, through a junction object
There is no relationship between the two objects
questions.explain: The lesson states OpportunityLineItem is a Master-Detail child of Opportunity.

questions.q: Per this lesson's four-step reading process, what should you do first when handed a request like 'opportunity revenue by product'?
options: Start at the object the request is actually about -- here, OpportunityLineItem, since it already connects an Opportunity to a product-level amount
Immediately write and run a SOQL query without checking the data model
Start with the Account object regardless of what was asked
Delete unrelated objects to simplify the model first
questions.explain: Step 1 is starting at the object the request is actually about, not an arbitrary object.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say to check for a 'missing junction' as one of the reading steps?
options: Because a many-to-many relationship hiding in a request needs a junction object in between -- missing that changes how you'd have to query it
Because junction objects are always visible without any checking needed
Because every data model always requires at least one junction object
Because junction objects are irrelevant to reading a data model
questions.explain: Recognizing a many-to-many relationship means expecting a junction object in between, per Lesson 23's pattern.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the real cost of skipping the reading process and writing a query directly from half-memorized field names?
options: The query may run and return a number that's subtly wrong -- silently dropping records through an optional Lookup or double-counting through an unexpected many-to-many
The query will always fail to execute with a clear error
There is no real cost -- it's always just as safe as reading the model first
Salesforce automatically validates and corrects incorrect assumptions before running any query
questions.explain: The lesson's core warning is that an incorrect but successfully-running query is the real danger, not an obvious failure.

questions.q: In this lesson's model, how does an OpportunityLineItem connect to a Product?
options: Indirectly, through a PricebookEntry
Directly, via a single ProductId field with no intermediate object
Through the junction object CampaignMember
Line items and Products are not related at all in this model
questions.explain: The lesson states each OpportunityLineItem has a PricebookEntryId, which in turn ties back to a Product.
